SRC62JOSEPH.title: Sacred Congregation of Rites, Novis hisce temporibus, 13 November 1962; effective 8 December 1962
SRC62JOSEPH.language: French translation of contemporary original Latin decree

records.topic: Scripture's inspiration versus approved liturgical wording
records.authorArgument: Lanslots describes nonbiblical Institution-text words as apostolic tradition equally inspired as Scripture.
records.criticalAnalysis: The approved liturgy has ecclesiastical authority, but not every liturgical composition shares the special canonical inspiration of the biblical books.
records.frenchSubstantiveDraft: Les paroles liturgiques approuvées possèdent une autorité ecclésiale, sans que toute composition liturgique bénéficie de l'inspiration propre aux livres canoniques.

records.topic: The holy Angel in Supplices te rogamus
records.authorArgument: Lanslots attributes a Christological interpretation to Guéranger, then also sets out a created-angel reading and admits uncertainty about the angel's identity.
records.criticalAnalysis: Attribute the respective readings and their reasons. Do not assert that an individual angel's identity is dogmatically settled or that the Host is physically transported to Heaven.
records.frenchSubstantiveDraft: Guéranger interprète l'Ange comme le Christ envoyé par le Père; Lanslots expose aussi l'hypothèse d'un ange créé. L'identification précise n'est pas définie par cette prière.

records.authorArgument: Lanslots explains Bellarmine's new consecration language as a renewed sacramental signification in the ritual union of the already consecrated Species.
records.criticalAnalysis: This must never be described as another Eucharistic consecration or second transubstantiation. Compare FRG57 rather than creating a duplicate explanation.
records.frenchSubstantiveDraft: La « nouvelle consécration » de cette explication désigne un sens sacramentel renouvelé et non une seconde transsubstantiation.

records.authorArgument: Lanslots says the Mass had been offered in Latin from apostolic times, while also discussing Eastern liturgical languages.
records.criticalAnalysis: Do not promote an unverified apostolic Latin chronology. Discuss historical rationale for Latin separately from earliest Christian liturgical languages.
records.frenchSubstantiveDraft: La défense du latin comme langue liturgique ne démontre pas que la Messe ait été célébrée exclusivement en latin depuis l'âge apostolique.

records.topic: Named intercessions for deceased outside ecclesial communion
records.authorArgument: Lanslots discusses historical diptychs, public remembrance and the distinct possibility of private supplication.
records.criticalAnalysis: Distinguish public liturgical naming, funerals, Mass intentions and private prayer. His 1897 canonical summaries are not universal current or 1962 directives.
records.frenchSubstantiveDraft: Il faut distinguer la mention publique au Canon, les funérailles, l'intention de Messe et la prière privée; les conclusions disciplinaires de 1897 n'ont pas valeur de règle universelle actuelle.

records.topic: Leviticus 8:14 and hands extended over Hanc igitur
records.authorArgument: Lanslots expressly applies the Old Testament laying-on-of-hands episode to the celebrant's prayer over the offerings.
records.criticalAnalysis: This biblical typology does not establish the historical origin of the prescribed Roman gesture or change the 1962 action sequence.
records.frenchSubstantiveDraft: Lv 8,14 offre une comparaison typologique; il ne prouve pas l'origine historique du geste prescrit par les rubriques romaines.

records.authorArgument: Lanslots treats Melchisedech's presentation of bread and wine as a sacrificial type and cites Psalm 109:4.
records.criticalAnalysis: Keep the accepted Eucharistic typology, but distinguish Genesis 14:18's biblical account from added assumptions about the exact ancient liturgical rite.
records.frenchSubstantiveDraft: La typologie eucharistique de Melchisédech ne permet pas de déduire de Gn 14,18 le détail d'un rite de consécration antique.

records.topic: Alexander I and the history of Canon formulas
records.authorArgument: Lanslots attributes a chronological Institution-narrative phrase to Pope Alexander I.
records.criticalAnalysis: Record this as a dated historical attribution requiring independent early manuscripts, not an established fact about who authored a section of the Canon.
records.frenchSubstantiveDraft: L'attribution d'une formule du Canon à Alexandre Ier doit être vérifiée dans les témoins liturgiques anciens avant publication.

records.authorArgument: Lanslots quotes Psalm 103 and 1 Corinthians 10:17 on bread and wine, participation, and the unity of the Church.
records.criticalAnalysis: An authentic theological theme, but this verse is absent from the actual Latin Offertory prayer at that moment; keep it in formation or thematic commentary, not invented in-text priest action.
records.frenchSubstantiveDraft: Un seul pain et un seul corps éclairent la communion ecclésiale; cette explication n'ajoute ni parole ni geste à l'Offertoire.

records.topic: St Joseph omitted from the 1897 Communicantes, inserted in the Roman Canon in late 1962
records.authorArgument: Lanslots transcribes the Communicantes names from the nineteenth-century Roman Canon, going directly from the Blessed Virgin to the apostles and martyrs without St Joseph.
records.criticalAnalysis: The Sacred Congregation of Rites' Novis hisce temporibus (13 November 1962) directed the insertion of 'sed et beati Ioseph eiusdem Virginis Sponsi', effective 8 December 1962. Its absence in Lanslots or Guéranger is not evidence that the current 1962-form Mass should omit Joseph. The original 1962 Missal printing date and subsequent amendment must be distinguished.
records.frenchSubstantiveDraft: Le Communicantes reproduit par Lanslots en 1897 ne nomme pas saint Joseph. Le décret Novis hisce temporibus du 13 novembre 1962 prescrivit son insertion, effective le 8 décembre 1962. Son absence dans un ouvrage antérieur n'est pas une rubrique pour la Messe célébrée selon l'usage romain de 1962 ainsi amendé.

acceptanceRules: The literal claim is attributed to Lanslots, while the critical analysis and counterclaim cite an independent source if used doctrinally.
Preconciliar Leo XIII and Pius XII already distinguish canonical biblical inspiration from ecclesiastical composition; this is not a Vatican II doctrinal invention.
Both interpretations of the holy Angel must be accurately presented, not turned into one settled identity.
1962 actions and roles must always be sourced separately from 1897 mystical interpretations.
Each paragraph of future published commentary requires linked original source evidence and French review.
No approval before scanned-page collation, claim-level deduplication and editorial release acceptance.
